title: Kumamoto & Aso in 3 Days — Kumamoto Castle, Aso, Suizenji
subtitle: Kumamoto Castle, a day tour to Aso and Suizenji, in and out of Aso Kumamoto Airport
summary: Three days in Kumamoto: Kumamoto Castle, Suizenji Jōjuen Garden and the city's food, with one day in the middle on a day tour to Aso. The notes include how to do Aso yourself by public transport. Depending on the alert level, Nakadake crater may not be approachable, and the day tour's itinerary can change on the day. The stay is written as the Tōrichō-suji and Shimotōri area, handy for the streetcar.

Could not be confirmed from official sources — check before you go
Winter opening hours for Aso Nakadake Crater and whether it is open on the day; day-tour itinerary details and prices.

Opening hours for Tsuruya, Katsuretei Shinshigai Main Branch, AMU PLAZA Kumamoto, the grounds of Aso Shrine, restaurants at Kusasenri, the Kumamoto City Hall observation corridor, Katō Shrine and the Luffy statue.
Actual limousine bus times and fares (the fare page on the official site could not be loaded, so the airport site's 2026 figures are used).
Whether buses and trains in Kumamoto Prefecture take transit IC cards: the travel log's Nov 2024 update says cash only; not checked against an official source.
Changes and trade-offs
This template takes only the Kumamoto and Aso part of the travel log (second half of day 5 to day 10); the Fukuoka part has its own template.
The travel log began on day 1 by JR from Fukuoka; this one flies in and out of Aso Kumamoto Airport instead, and squeezes the log's 5 days in Kumamoto into 3.
The travel log's author took buses and JR up Aso alone; by our rules this uses a day tour, with the public-transport alternative in the notes.
Depending on the alert level, Nakadake may be closed to the crater rim, and the day tour's itinerary can change on the day.
Travel time on the day tour and airport transfers exceeds the usual 30% share; that is the distance to Aso.
Travel log details

The stay is written as an area only: the log's author stayed at a hotel in Suizenji but rated it poorly, so it is written as the Tōrichō-suji and Shimotōri area, handy for the streetcar to Kumamoto Castle.
Entry and data
Register your immigration and customs declaration on Visit Japan Web before you leave: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
For data, use a physical SIM or an eSIM.
Airport to the city

From Aso Kumamoto Airport take the limousine bus (Kyushu Sanko): about 45 min to Sakuramachi Bus Terminal by express, about 50 min by regular service; about 60–65 min to Kumamoto Station; about 35 min to Suizenji-kōen-mae. The fare to Sakuramachi and Kumamoto Station is around ¥1,400, to Suizenji-kōen-mae around ¥1,000.
The official site shows about 31 express and 41 Kumamoto Station services a day, and a timetable change from 1 Nov 2026 — check the latest timetable before you go.
A taxi takes about 45 min and around ¥6,100 to Kumamoto Station, and about 40 min and around ¥5,700 to Sakuramachi (official estimates, tolls not included).
Buses can run late; the travel log recorded one arriving nearly 10 minutes late in 2023.
Getting around Kumamoto

The city runs mainly on streetcars and buses. The travel log's 2024 update says many bus companies in Kumamoto Prefecture and Kumamoto Electric Railway no longer take transit IC cards such as Suica, so carry yen in cash and check the current situation.
Buses are mostly boarded at the rear and exited at the front: take a numbered ticket and pay by number when you get off; the driver gives no change, but you can change money on board.
Aso day tour
Several operators run this day tour from Kumamoto (covering Nakadake, Kusasenri and Aso Shrine); compare itineraries, meeting points and whether lunch is included before you go.

Access to Aso Nakadake Crater is restricted by the volcanic alert level; the official site showed level 2 in Sep 2026, with entry within 1 km of the crater banned. Check https://aso-volcano.jp/ before you go to see whether you can reach the rim; when you cannot, the day tour usually views it from a distance.

Doing it yourself by public transport: from Kumamoto Kōtsū Center (Sakuramachi Bus Terminal) take the Kyushu Sanko Asosan-jō line to Asosan-jō bus terminal, then the Aso crater shuttle to the crater; or take the JR Hōhi Line to Aso Station and then the Aso Tozan line bus up. Check frequencies and fares on the Kyushu Sanko site https://www.sankobus.jp/ .

What the travel log's author did: Aso Station to the top took about 40 min, with Kusasenri on the way; the JR local back to Kumamoto took about 1 h 45 min, with few trains, and missing one could mean a one-hour wait. Aso is a small station and the JR station may not take electronic payment.
Booking and timing
Book the day tour a few days before you go.
Kumamon Square show times change every month, with no show on Tuesdays; check the calendar before deciding the order of day 3: https://kumamon-land.jp/squares/
Kumamoto Castle tickets can be bought in advance at Sakura-no-baba Jōsaien to skip the queue at the keep entrance; suitcases are not allowed inside the keep.
Other
Carry enough yen in cash: some small shops, buses and small stations do not take cards.
Parts of Kumamoto Castle are still under restoration; the main keep has been restored and is open.

Adjust the airport time on the last day to your actual flight; the travel log says in 2023 the international counters opened only about 2 hours before departure, and the 3rd-floor restaurants are after security but before departure.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 3 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Aso Kumamoto Airport, with all three nights in central Kumamoto. You get around the city by streetcar and on foot, and Aso is a day tour, so nobody has to drive.

Day 1: land around midday, take the airport limousine bus into town, have Kumamoto ramen around Shimotōri, then spend the afternoon at {@d1-03}. Tsuruya for Kumamon goods at dusk, and horse sashimi and karashi renkon at an izakaya in the evening.
Day 2: a day tour up to Aso for the Nakadake Crater and Kusasenri-ga-hama, then {@d2-04} and the shopping street in front of it. Back in Kumamoto, dinner at AMU PLAZA by the station.
Day 3: {@d3-01} in the morning, the Kumamon Square stage show, tonkatsu at Katsuretei for lunch, and a rest in the Sakuramachi rooftop garden before the bus back to the airport.
Where to sleep: all three nights around Tōrichō-suji and Shimotōri in central Kumamoto, a short streetcar ride from the castle and close to dinner and shopping.

Getting around: the limousine bus links the airport and the city in about 35 to 65 minutes depending on your stop. In town it is streetcars and buses, and some buses do not take transit IC cards, so carry yen in cash. Book the Aso day tour a few days ahead; whether you can walk to the crater rim depends on the volcano alert level that day. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants Kumamoto Castle, Kumamon and the Aso volcano in three days without driving. It works solo or with a small group; the city days are light on walking, while the Aso day is mostly on the coach.
